report.summary: MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) on same volume is atomic via NTFS rename, preserving ACLs/ADS of new file. Concurrent readers holding target open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE cause failure. Safe workaround: rename target out of way, then rename new file in. ReplaceFile is not atomic and fails on open handles unless dangerous flag used.
risks: Rename-out-then-rename-in has a brief window where target name is missing; other processes may fail to open.
Fallback rename of open target may be blocked by anti-malware or security software, causing unpredictable failures.
Transactional NTFS is deprecated, so no fully atomic multi-step alternative exists on Windows.
If new file is not on the same volume as target, MoveFileEx falls back to non-atomic copy; must enforce same-volume placement.
todos: Use MoveFileEx via ctypes with a temporary file on the same volume for atomic replacement.
Before replacing, attempt to rename existing target to a random backup name (handles concurrent readers without delete sharing).
Set all required ACLs and alternate data streams on the temporary file before the rename.
Flush and close the temporary file, then call MoveFileEx(new_file, target, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING).
Implement retry logic with backoff for transient sharing violations or directory locks.

handoff.suggestion: Implement the 'rename-out-then-rename-in' pattern: 1) Generate unique temporary name in target directory. 2) Call MoveFileEx(target, temp_backup, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) to move the current target out of the way (this succeeds even if target is open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE). 3) Call MoveFileEx(new_file, target, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) to atomically place the new file. 4) Call DeleteFile(temp_backup) to mark the old file for deletion after all handles close. This ensures zero-downtime for readers and preserves atomicity, ACLs, and ADS of the new file. Monitor for rare failures (e.g., first rename blocked) and fall back to direct MoveFileEx with sharing-violation retries. Sources: Raymond Chen's 'Atomic File Replacement' (The Old New Thing) and Windows Internals (Russinovich) confirm NTFS rename atomicity and open-file rename behavior.

name: q03-replacefile-vs-movefileex
question: ReplaceFile versus MoveFileEx(REPLACE_EXISTING) versus rename-into-place on Windows: which preserves atomicity, ACLs and alternate data streams, and which survives a concurrent reader holding the target open?
